module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Lacunary Sequences in Real Number Fields

The following problems were proposed and discussed by Dubickas as Conjecture 2 in [Dub09].

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Dub09] Dubickas, Artūras. "An approximation property of lacunary sequences."
    Israel Journal of Mathematics 170.1 (2009): 95-111.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Bugeaud05

open Filter

/--
Problem 10.5 (first part). Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a real number field. Then, for any
$\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a lacunary sequence $(t_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of positive numbers
in $\mathbb{K}$ such that
$$\limsup_{n \to \infty} \{\xi t_n\} \ge 1 - \varepsilon,$$
for any real number $\xi$ not in $\mathbb{K}$.

This follows from the stronger `problem_10_5_moreover` via
`problem_10_5_of_moreover`. A Lean 4 formalization by Kenta Kitamura
([KitaKen1 on GitHub](https://github.com/KitaKen1)) is available at
[KitaKen1/bugeaud-10-5-lacunary](https://github.com/KitaKen1/bugeaud-10-5-lacunary).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/bugeaud-10-5-lacunary/blob/fa5533b0229a19f2092c777cadb43ef4b0f2600b/lean/Bugeaud105/Compatibility.lean#L18-L19"]
theorem problem_10_5 (K : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) [FiniteDimensional ℚ K]
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ t : ℕ → K, (∀ n, 0 < (t n : ℝ)) ∧
      IsLacunaryReal (fun k => (t k : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ ξ : ℝ, ξ ∉ K →
        (1 - ε) ≤ limsup (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Problem 10.5 ("moreover" clause). With the same hypotheses as `problem_10_5`, the
sequence $(t_n)$ can be chosen so that, for any real $\xi$ not in $\mathbb{K}$, each
subinterval of $[0, 1]$ of length $\varepsilon$ contains a limit point of the sequence
$(\{\xi t_n\})_{n \ge 1}$. This is strictly stronger than `problem_10_5`: the limsup
bound is the special case at the subinterval $[1 - \varepsilon, 1]$.

A Lean 4 formalization by Kenta Kitamura
([KitaKen1 on GitHub](https://github.com/KitaKen1)) proves this statement using the
explicit positive integer sequence
$$t_{Jk+r} = (J+r)2^k \qquad (k \ge 0,\ 0 \le r < J).$$
Here $Q$ is a positive integer chosen so that $Q > 1/\varepsilon$, and $J = 10Q!$.
Since $\mathbb{K}$ contains $\mathbb{Q}$, every term belongs to $\mathbb{K}$.
The proof verifies that this sequence is lacunary and has the required cluster-point
property simultaneously for every $\xi \notin \mathbb{K}$. See
[KitaKen1/bugeaud-10-5-lacunary](https://github.com/KitaKen1/bugeaud-10-5-lacunary).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/bugeaud-10-5-lacunary/blob/fa5533b0229a19f2092c777cadb43ef4b0f2600b/lean/Bugeaud105/Compatibility.lean#L14-L16"]
theorem problem_10_5_moreover (K : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ) [FiniteDimensional ℚ K]
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ t : ℕ → K, (∀ n, 0 < (t n : ℝ)) ∧
      IsLacunaryReal (fun k => (t k : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ ξ : ℝ, ξ ∉ K → ∀ a, a ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (1 - ε) →
        ∃ y ∈ Set.Icc a (a + ε),
          MapClusterPt y atTop (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/-- The "moreover" form of Problem 10.5 implies the first part: applying the cluster-point
density to the subinterval $[1 - \varepsilon, 1]$ yields the required lower bound on the
limsup. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_5_of_moreover (h : type_of% problem_10_5_moreover) :
    type_of% problem_10_5 := by
  intro K _ ε hε
  obtain ⟨t, hpos, hlac, hξ⟩ := h K hε
  refine ⟨t, hpos, hlac, fun ξ hξK => ?_⟩
  have hb : IsBoundedUnder (· ≤ ·) atTop (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) :=
    isBoundedUnder_of ⟨1, fun n => (Int.fract_lt_one (ξ * (t n : ℝ))).le⟩
  by_cases hε1 : ε ≤ 1
  · obtain ⟨y, hy, hcluster⟩ := hξ ξ hξK (1 - ε) ⟨by linarith, le_refl _⟩
    have hb_ge : IsBoundedUnder (· ≥ ·) atTop (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) :=
      isBoundedUnder_of ⟨0, fun n => Int.fract_nonneg (ξ * (t n : ℝ))⟩
    have hcob : IsCoboundedUnder (· ≤ ·) atTop (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) :=
      hb_ge.isCoboundedUnder_le
    have hle : y ≤ limsup (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) atTop := by
      rw [Filter.le_limsup_iff hcob hb]
      exact fun a ha => MapClusterPt.frequently hcluster (eventually_gt_nhds ha)
    linarith [hy.1]
  · push Not at hε1
    have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ limsup (fun n => Int.fract (ξ * (t n : ℝ))) atTop :=
      le_limsup_of_frequently_le
        ((Filter.Eventually.of_forall
          fun n => Int.fract_nonneg (ξ * (t n : ℝ))).frequently) hb
    linarith

end Bugeaud05

reformulations.difference: Lacunarity is encoded by `IsLacunaryReal`: there is c > 1 with c·t_k < t_{k+1} for all sufficiently large k (strict inequality, only eventually), and the sequence is indexed from 0. Dubickas (p. 95) defines lacunary as: there is a > 1 with t_{n+1} ≥ a·t_n for every positive integer n (t_1, t_2, ...). The limsup is Mathlib's `Filter.limsup` in ℝ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an existence statement the two conventions agree. (⇒) Take a Lean witness and drop the first N terms, where N comes from the `eventually`. Positivity is kept, t_{n+1} > c·t_n gives the source's non-strict condition for every n, and the limsup does not change under a shift (`Filter.limsup_nat_add`). (⇐) If a source witness has t_{n+1} ≥ a·t_n with t_n > 0, then ((1+a)/2)·t_n < t_{n+1} for every n. Because the fractional parts lie in [0,1), Mathlib's limsup in ℝ is the genuine limsup, so `1 - ε ≤ limsup` means exactly limsup{ξt_n} ≥ 1−ε. I proved this in /workspace/review/equiv.lean as `first_iff : type_of% Bugeaud05.problem_10_5 ↔ Literal1`, where Literal1 uses Dubickas's for-every-n condition t_{n+1} ≥ a·t_n. It needs only the standard axioms and does not use the external proof.

reformulations.difference: The Lean version asks, for every a ∈ [0, 1−ε], for a `MapClusterPt` (a subsequential limit) y in the CLOSED interval [a, a+ε] ⊆ [0,1], so y = 1 is allowed. Dubickas asks that each subinterval of [0,1) of length ε contain an accumulation point of the sequence {ξt_n}. It uses the same eventual-lacunarity convention as `problem_10_5`. At one fixed ε, the closed-interval condition is slightly weaker than the open-interval reading: a cluster set spaced exactly ε apart meets every closed interval of length ε but not every open one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The theorem quantifies over all ε > 0, and as families over ε the two are equivalent. Source ⇒ Lean at the same ε: every such [a, a+ε] contains a subinterval of [0,1) of length ε (an open or half-open one). Lean at ε/2 ⇒ source at ε: every subinterval of [0,1) of length ε contains [b+ε/4, b+3ε/4], and limsup ≥ 1−ε/2 ≥ 1−ε. Cluster point versus accumulation point of the set of values: for ξ ∉ K, {ξt_n} = {ξt_m} with t_n ≠ t_m would give ξ = integer/(t_n − t_m) ∈ K. An eventually increasing sequence takes each value only finitely often. So each fractional-part value occurs only finitely often, and the two notions coincide. I proved in Lean `moreover_iff : type_of% Bugeaud05.problem_10_5_moreover ↔ Literal2`, where Literal2 uses Dubickas's for-every-n lacunarity and the strongest reading of the source: every OPEN (a, a+ε) with 0 ≤ a and a+ε ≤ 1 contains a cluster point. Only standard axioms are used. The cluster-point versus accumulation-point step is argued on paper, not in Lean.

review.notes:
What I found: no misformalization. Both theorems state Dubickas's Conjecture 2, which Bugeaud reproduces as Problem 10.5: first the limsup part, then the 'moreover' part. The quantifier order is ∀K ∀ε ∃t ∀ξ ∉ K, as in the source. `IntermediateField ℚ ℝ` with `[FiniteDimensional ℚ K]` is exactly a real number field. A non-real number field E reduces to E ∩ ℝ, since both t_n and ξ are real. `Int.fract` is the fractional part {·}. `problem_10_5_of_moreover` is a valid, fully proved implication.

Why a surprisingly easy proof is not a red flag here: the statement has an elementary proof. The block sequence t_{Jk+r} = (J+r)2^k with J = 10·Q! and Q > 1/ε works for every irrational ξ. For infinitely many k, the distance from Q!ξ2^k to the nearest integer is at least 1/4; combined with Dirichlet's theorem, this makes the multiples jξ2^k with J ≤ j < 2J hit every interval of length ε. I checked this argument by hand. The ease belongs to the conjecture as posed, not to the formalization. Dubickas himself remarks 'it is sufficient to prove the conjecture for E = ℚ', which is exactly the reduction the proof uses. He also wrote that 'the smallest known ε for which the conjecture holds is ε = 1/2', so the elementary construction was apparently overlooked at the time.

Status: the external proof pins formal-conjectures commit b86fdb9a. The statements there are byte-identical to HEAD (only docstrings and attributes changed), and `Lacunary.lean` is unchanged. That proof uses the same Lean v4.33.1 and Mathlib rev 0df444a as this checkout. I concatenated its modules into a scratch file importing this module. It compiles, `example : type_of% Bugeaud05.problem_10_5_moreover := Bugeaud105.problem_10_5_moreover` and the matching `problem_10_5` example type-check, and `#print axioms` shows only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The `research solved` tags and both `formal_proof` links (Compatibility.lean lines 14–16 and 18–19) are therefore accurate. The docstring's description of the sequence matches `blockSeq`.

Minor wording notes, not defects: the moreover docstring says '[0, 1]' and 'limit point' where Dubickas says '[0, 1)' and 'accumulation point'; these are equivalent as a family over ε (see reformulations). I could not see Bugeaud's own wording of Problem 10.5: the chapter is paywalled and Google Books blocked automated access. So I checked faithfulness against Dubickas's original Conjecture 2, the source the file cites as the problem's origin. The docstring's version of Bugeaud's wording agrees with it. `[FiniteDimensional ℚ K]` is not needed by the proof, but including it matches the source.
